title: In conversation with Edward Chang
abstract: As part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Edward Chang, Margaret Liu Collins and Edward B. Collins distinguished Professor and Chair of neurosurgery at the University of California, San Francisco, about the evolution of speech brain–computer interfaces (BCIs). He discusses how advances in AI are accelerating the translation of BCIs into the clinic, the challenge of restoring natural communication, and why large-scale neural datasets may ultimately help build computational models of the human brain.
abstract_zh: 作为我们神经技术专题专栏的一部分，我们与加州大学旧金山分校神经外科 Margaret Liu Collins 和 Edward B. Collins 杰出教授兼主任爱德华·昌进行了交流。他讨论了人工智能进步如何加速脑机接口（BCI）向临床的转化，恢复自然交流的挑战，以及大规模神经数据集最终如何有助于构建人类大脑的计算模型。
